chunks.arabic_text: ٢٥ - مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، الصَّائِغُ، أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ، كُوفِيٌّ. غَالٍ، ضَعِيفٌ، لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ.

translations.en: 25 – Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, al-Sa'igh (the jeweler), Abu Ja'far. Kufan. A ghali, weak, he is not turned to.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* highlights Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sa'id, a Kufan jeweler whose profession is often cited as a marker of his social standing and potential for independent judgment. Classified as 'ghali' (an exaggerator of the Imams' virtues) and 'da'eef' (weak), his narrations are considered less reliable due to these theological and biographical traits, reflecting the rigorous scrutiny applied to Kufan transmitters in Shia hadith sciences.
en.seo_question: Who is Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sa'id al-Sa'igh and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.غَالٍ: Ghali (one who exaggerates the virtues or divinity of the Imams)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Da'if (weak, referring to the reliability of a narrator)
key_terms.الصَّائِغُ: Al-Sa'igh (the jeweler, a kunya or occupational title)
